caveats: Padmanābha's astrolabe manual (1423 CE), ch. I (Yantrarājādhikāra), survives in two Lucknow MSS; the complete Sanskrit text and translation is Ohashi, IJHS 32.3 (1997) — an image scan, so shloka fields are empty pending an OCR proofread (nothing retyped).

Star identifications follow Pai & Shylaja, 'The southern stars identified in Indian astronomical catalogues', JApA 41:20 (2020), who single out these two names as first attestations — Sanskrit formations, not translations from the Arabic.

entries.translation_en: Aśvamukha, the horse's face, among the stars of the astrolabe table.
entries.identification_notes: First attestation of the name — a Sanskrit formation, not an Arabic translation (Pai & Shylaja 2020). The kneeling Hercules' head star read as a horse's face. Coordinates reduce to α Her.

entries.translation_en: Toraṇa, the arched gateway, among the stars of the astrolabe table.
entries.identification_notes: First attestation, a Sanskrit formation (Pai & Shylaja 2020): the Serpent's neck star as a toraṇa, the festal arch. The Sarvasiddhāntarāja later carries the region as Sarpaśīrṣa.
